title: A Cover for the Border Revisited
premise: Elodie Lockridge, a veteran interpreter for a fractious peace delegation, is approached by Marek Voss, a man who claims she once saved his life in Sarajevo — a favor she has no memory of performing. The debt he repays is information: the delegation's ceasefire talks are a staged cover for an extraction of a high-value defector, and Elodie's linguistic access makes her indispensable to people who intend to leave no loose ends. As she helps smuggle the defector, Ana Kessler, across a collapsing border, Elodie discovers Ana may be deliberate bait designed to flush out a mole inside the delegation — possibly Marek himself. In the end, Elodie chooses love over duty by burning her own credibility to expose the mole, lets Ana go free rather than deliver her to either side, and walks away from the delegation with Marek, carrying a new memory worth keeping.
about_author: August Vane is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent six years in Balkan and Caucasus border regions before turning to fiction. Vane writes thrillers about people whose professions require them to be trusted and whose survival requires them not to be.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. During a tedious translation session in Geneva, a stranger named Marek Voss corners her and claims she saved his life in Sarajevo ten years ago — a debt she cannot recall. He leaves her a card and a warning: watch the delegation's security chief. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional composure.

chapters.title: Rules Rewritten
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She investigates her own archives and finds a gap: one week of her Sarajevo deployment unaccounted for, redacted even from her own records. Her supervisor, Halloran, deflects smoothly. Emotional beat: the first crack in her trust of the institution that defined her.

chapters.title: Terms of Art
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek reveals himself as an ex-intelligence officer now working private extraction. He explains the peace talks are cover for moving defector Ana Kessler out through the border corridor Elodie will interpret along. He offers her a choice, not an order. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: The Delegation Sings
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the opening plenary, Elodie notices the delegations' translators are being fed subtly different texts — someone is engineering mistranslation to stall talks. She says nothing, cataloguing who benefits. Emotional beat: the interpreter's loneliness of knowing what everyone meant.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Marek shows her surveillance photos proving she's already being watched by the delegation's own security detail. The favor-that-never-happened becomes leverage either way: help him, or be implicated. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ana Kessler, On Paper
chapters.summary: Ana's POV. Introduced inside the safe house, Ana rehearses her defection story and we learn she suspects she's bait but doesn't know for whom. She studies Elodie's photograph. Emotional beat: cold clarity of a woman pricing her own life.

chapters.title: Border Weather
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The delegation travels to the frontier town of Velika Most for the signing phase. Elodie maps the crossing points under cover of advance interpretation work, and Marek appears in her hotel bar wearing another man's name. Emotional beat: complicity becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: What Sarajevo Left Out
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Elodie's POV. A fragmented memory surfaces: a rainy checkpoint, a wounded teenager, a decision made in three seconds that someone later erased. She still can't see the face. Emotional beat: grief for a self she can't verify.

chapters.title: Halloran's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Halloran's POV. We enter the mind of the security chief: he knows about Marek, suspects Elodie, and reports to someone above the delegation. He calculates that losing Ana at the border is acceptable if it exposes the leak. Emotional beat: bureaucratic ruthlessness.

chapters.title: A Room With Two Exits
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Marek lays out the extraction plan: forty-eight hours, a river crossing, forged papers sewn into Ana's coat lining. Elodie must mis-translate a key security briefing to buy them the window. Emotional beat: the point of no return crossed quietly, over coffee.

chapters.title: The Mistranslation
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the live session, Elodie softens a patrol-schedule disclosure by seconds of phrasing — enough. A junior linguist catches the discrepancy and hesitates. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration braided together; ten years of rules spent in one sentence.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Ana's POV. Ana finds a tracker sewn into her own luggage — placed before she ever reached the safe house. Whoever runs her wants her followed. She tells Elodie, forcing the plan to fork. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as proof of worth.

chapters.title: Three Names on a List
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek narrows the mole to three candidates inside the delegation, and one of the names shakes him: someone from his old service. He begins lying to Elodie by omission. Emotional beat: love against duty, from the other side of the glass.

chapters.title: Velika Most After Dark
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. First extraction attempt fails — the river crossing is pre-watched. They escape on foot through the flooded market district, and Elodie realizes only three people could have known the route. Emotional beat: adrenaline curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Junior Linguist
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie confronts Petra, the junior linguist who caught the mistranslation, expecting blackmail — instead finding a frightened idealist who reveals Halloran ordered her to watch Elodie. But Petra also saw someone else in the archive room. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: Confession at the Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Under pressure, Marek admits the truth about Sarajevo: there was no favor. He invented the debt because Elodie was the only uncorrupted channel left, and guilt was the fastest way to reach her. Emotional beat: the cruelest honesty; love built on a fabricated foundation tested.

chapters.title: The Real Defector
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Reassembling the redacted week, Elodie realizes the true prize isn't Ana — it's the evidence Ana carries naming the mole, and the mole is Halloran's superior inside the delegation itself. Ana isn't bait for Marek; she's bait for Elodie. Emotional beat: vertigo of being the target all along.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes at the Crossing
chapters.summary: Climax part one, multiple POVs interwoven. The second crossing goes live: fog, a patrol gone rogue, Halloran arriving to take custody of Ana 'for her protection.' Marek draws the patrol; Elodie takes Ana downriver. Emotional beat: everything converging at speed.

chapters.title: Interpreter's Privilege
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Elodie's POV. Cornered at the rail bridge, Elode does the one thing no one can undo: she broadcasts, open-channel, a verbatim translation of the evidence in Ana's possession — making the mole's name public in three languages simultaneously. Emotional beat: duty inverted into weapon.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.summary: Halloran's POV, final entry. Halloran's superiors cut him loose within the hour; he faces ruin with the strange relief of a man finally off the clock. He lets Elodie walk, one professional acknowledging another. Emotional beat: hollow victory on both sides.

chapters.title: A Debt Repaid Differently
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie gives Ana the forged papers and sends her west alone — free of every handler, including Marek's clients. She resigns from the delegation by leaving her accreditation badge on the plenary table mid-session. Emotional beat: quiet, costly liberation.

chapters.title: New Memory, Kept
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, epilogue. Months later, in a coastal town far from any border, Elodie and Marek begin building something without institutional shadow. When he asks why she forgave the invented favor, she answers: everyone needs a first memory they choose themselves. Emotional beat: belonging, finally self-authored.
